<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|374||}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|The Svmme of the Actes of the Apostles, Conteining Specially the Gestes of the Tvvo Principal}} Apostles, SS. Peter and Paul, in such order of time and yeres of the Emperours, and from Christs Natiuitie, and Ascension, as they vvere done: so far as by holy Scriptures or Ecclesiastical vvriters may be gathered.}}}}

Wherein though it be not possible to set dovvne the precise and vndoubted time or yere of euery thing, because neither S. Luke nor others do note particularly and orderly the moments of euery action of the said Apostles: yet vve folovv the most probable and plaine plat that vve finde in holy Scripture and auncient vvriters.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''See the annot. Rom. 16, 15. Gal. 1.''}} Whereby the studious reader may easily discouer the foly of the Protestants, that can finde no time vvhen * Peter might possibly come to Rome, be Bishop, and die there: diuers things in S. Paules actes being no lesse hard to reconcile to the course of S. Lukes narration, then any thing touching the historie of S. Peter, namely his * three yeres preaching in Arabia: al vvhich must needes be true, vvhether vve hit the very iust time or no, and hovv so euer authors differ about the same.

| style='vertical-align: top;' | {{dropinitial|P}}ETER causeth the Disciples to procede to the election of an other Apostle in Iudas roome. ''Act. 1.''

| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | Receiuing vvith the rest the gifts of the Holy Ghost on Whitsunday, he made the first Sermon, and conuerted 3000. ''Act. 2.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He cureth one borne lame, preacheth Christ and penance to the Ievves: so that 5000 beleeued. ''Act. 3 & 4.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He is imprisoned, released againe, threatened and commaunded to preache no more: but he vvith Iohn ansvvereth, that they must obey God more then man. ''Act. 4.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He striketh to death vvith a vvord, Ananias and Saphira, for sacrilege. ''Act. 5.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He is sent vvith Iohn to Samaria, to confirme the nevvly baptized, vvhere he reproueth Simon Magus. ''Act. 8.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 19
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 35
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 2
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He healeth Aeneas at Lydda, and raiseth Tabitha from death at Ioppe. ''Act. 9.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He is vvarned and taught by a vision, to preach to Cornelius a Gentil. ''Act. 10.'' He defendeth his receiuing of the Gentiles ''Act. 11.'' and recordeth ''(Act. 15)'' that God called the first Gentiles by his ministerie, so that Paules first preaching to them, and his going to Arabia, must be after this. ''See S. Chrys. in Act. ho. 22. Euseb. li. 2 c. 3.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 20
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 36
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 3
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He continueth preaching in diuers partes of Iurie and the prouinces adioyning. About tvvo yeres after this, S. Paul visiteth him at Hierusalem. ''Gal. 1.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He preacheth in Syria and the Prouinces of Asia minor, Bythynia, Pontus, Galatia, Cappodocia, ordaining Bishops and Priests in diuers places. ''1 Pet. 1. Nicepho. li. 2 c. 35. Platina in Petro.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 23
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 39
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 6
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He goeth to Antioche, preaching there, and making that his Seate, yet not remaining there continually, but for the affaires of the Church, departing thence, sometime to Hierusalem, sometime to other places. ''Hiero. in Catalogo. Ignat. ad Magnesianos.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | At Hierusalem he is cast into prison after the putting of S. Iames to death, by the commaundement of Herod. he is praied for by the vvhole Church, & deliuered out of prison by an Angel. ''Act. 12.''
|-

| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 44
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 11
| style='vertical-align: top;' | Auoiding the furie of Herod, he leaueth Iurie againe. He appointeth Euodius Bishop in Antioche, ''Euseb. in Chron. & li. 2 c. 16. Suidas, Ignat. ad Antiochen.'' And passing by Corinth, {{sc|he came to Rome}}, to conuince Simon Magus. ''Hiero. in Catalogo. Euseb. li. 2 c. 12. 13. 24. Concil. to. 1.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He approueth & declareth the Gospel of S. Marke to be Canonical. ''Hiero. in Catalo. Euseb. li. 2 c. 14.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | Hauing founded the Church at Rome, and planted his Apostolical Seate there, aftervvard absent from the citie (either expelled thence vvith other Ievves, ''Cornel. Tacit. in Claudio:'' or rather according to the office of his Apostleship) leauing it for a time, he visited other Churches, and came to Hierusalem againe, vsing both in his absence and presence, Linus and Cletus for his coadiutors. ''To. 2 Concil. pag. 656, Epiph. to. 2. Haeres. 27.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 9
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 52
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' | 18
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He holdeth the first Councel. ''Act. 15.'' He is reprehended at Antioche by S. Paul. ''Galat. 1.'' except that difference fell before the Councel, as some thinke. ''August. ep. 19.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He returneth to Rome againe, the Romane faith by his diligence novv made famous through the vvorld. ''Ro. 1. & 15. Theodoret. in 16. Ro.'' Thence he vvriteth his first epistle. ''1 Pet. 5. Euseb. li. 2 c. 14. Hiero. in Catalogo.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He sendeth S. Marke to Alexandria, and others to plant the faith in diuers partes of the vvorld. ''Grego. li. 5 ep. 60. & li. 6 ep. 37. Nicepho. li. 2 c. 35.''
|-
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='text-align: right; vertical-align: top; padding-right: 8px;' |
| style='vertical-align: top;' | He vvriteth his second epistle a litle before his death, vvhich Christ reuealed to him to be at hand, ''2 Pet. 1.'' He taketh order for his successor.
|-
